statements.text: The task model carries a nullable `deletedAt` timestamp, serialized in JSON as `deletedAt` — an ISO-8601 string when set, `null` when the task is active.
`DELETE /tasks/{id}` soft-deletes: it sets `deletedAt` to the current time, retains the task in the store, and returns 204 No Content.
`DELETE /tasks/{id}` for an unknown id still returns 404 Not Found.
`GET /tasks` returns only active (not soft-deleted) tasks by default.
`GET /tasks?includeDeleted=true` returns all tasks, including soft-deleted ones whose `deletedAt` is non-null.
`GET /tasks/{id}` returns 404 Not Found for a soft-deleted task.
The four seeded tasks remain active (`deletedAt` = null) after startup — existing rows keep working (backward-compatible migration).
`dotnet build` and `dotnet test` stay green and the five pre-existing tests still pass.
The other CRUD endpoints (POST /tasks, PUT /tasks/{id}, GET /) keep their existing behaviour, and the change stays inside `src/TaskTracker.Api` and `tests/TaskTracker.Tests`.
